text:
Lee: Heads up — we're getting scheduling failures for production model-serving in us-west-2. Several pods stuck Pending with "0/40 nodes are available" and OOM-ish GPU allocation errors.

infra-bot: [Alert] Metric gpu.node_pool_utilization(us-west-2/gpu-pool-1) = 98% (5m avg). Cluster Autoscaler attempted scale-up 3x in last 10m and failed due to Capacity/PodAffinity constraints.

Ashley: Confirmed. kubectl describe pod shows: "failed to fit: node(s) didn't match Pod's nodeSelector/taints" and "Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu" on the schedulable nodes. Also seeing a bunch of small-req jobs bound to gpu:1 with strict nodeSelector for taint gpu:dedicated=true

sre-oncall: Any recent rollout or CI job that could've exploded GPU usage? Check for runaway training jobs.

Maria: There's an ad-hoc finetune job (finetune-78) launched from a notebook group about ~20m ago — it spawned 40 parallel worker pods each requesting 2 GPUs. That's prolly the spike.

Ops-Eng: Oof. That explains it. The cluster-autoscaler wanted to add nodes but the nodepool autoscaling template only offers g4dn.12xlarge which is tainted for "gpu:spot=true" and our pods require "gpu:dedicated=true" — mismatch -> CA gives up.

DevX: Quick mitigation steps: 1) suspend the finetune job; 2) cordon the spot nodepool so we stop scheduling more pods there; 3) scale up a dedicated GPU pool manually with matching taints.

Ben: I'm on suspending the job. Run: kubectl delete job finetune-78 --namespace=notebooks --grace-period=0 --force

Maria: Confirmed deletion started. Workers are terminating.

infra-bot: [Event] NodePool gpu-dedicated-usw2 has no more available capacity in cloud provider quota. Attempted manual create returned "quota_exceeded: GPUs".

Ashley: Now hitting cloud quota limits too. We need an emergency throttle on new GPU requests and a fallback routing policy — divert lower-priority requests to CPU-only inference or to eu-central-1 if acceptable.

Lee: Apply the emergency admission-control patch: set webhook to reject pods with label finetune=true and priority < 100000. That will stop accidental interactive jobs.

Ops-Eng: Patch applied (admission-control: gpu-emergency-throttle = true). Confirmed new finetune pods are being rejected with 403.

sre-oncall: While quota is being freed, let's evict low-priority model replicas to free GPUs for critical routes. Suggested command:

kubectl get pods -l service=model-serving,env=prod -o name | xargs -n1 -I{} kubectl patch {} -p '{"spec":{"priorityClassName":"low-priority"}}' --type=merge

Ben: I manually scaled down non-critical replicas for model-x and model-y: kubectl scale deployment model-x --replicas=2 -n prod

Maria: We're seeing GPUs return as finetune workers terminate. Cloud quota ticket submitted (ticket# 89421) to increase GPU quota in us-west-2.

infra-bot: [Alert] Cluster Autoscaler tip: some pods set nodeAffinity to dedicated-gpu but node template label is gpu-type=nvidia-tesla-t4 — mismatch. CA shows "No nodes match Pod affinity" in logs.

Ashley: Long-term fix: align nodepool labels/taints with typical pod selectors OR change scheduler constraints in our job launcher. I'll open a tracking PR to make notebook launcher set tolerations instead of hard nodeSelector.

Lee: Can we create a temporary pool using preemptible GPUs with the dedicated taint so CA can scale that up quickly (and we avoid quota conflict with spot pool)?

Ops-Eng: Cloud provider doesn't let mix of preemptible + dedicated in same quota slice. But we can request a soft increase; meanwhile we can move some workloads to eu-central-1 as a staged fallback. I pushed a route change to the traffic router for non-SLA tasks.

sre-oncall: Monitoring: latency SLO for model-serving spiked to 420ms -> 1.8s for some endpoints. After scale-down of non-critical replicas and finetune termination latency improved to 230ms.

DevX: Can we add an automated guard in the notebook service to prevent >8 GPUs per notebook group without explicit approval? Right now it's too easy to spawn 40-worker jobs.

Maria: Added feature request and an internal policy: default notebook quota = 4 GPUs. PR opened: notebooks/guard/PR#112. Also added guidance to the internal docs: links to quota workflows.

Ashley: Action items:
- short: tighten admission webhook + manual scale down (done)
- med: align node labels/taints and update autoscaler templates (tracking ticket TKT-701)
- med: notebook launcher change to tolerations (TKT-702)
- long: region quota monitoring + proactive GP quota requests (TKT-703)

Lee: Thanks all. Marking incident as mitigated. Will run a short postmortem doc and include timings and cost impact (estimate: ~0.6 GPU-hours of cross-region failover + quota request ticket details). :white_check_mark:

Ben: Logging timeline in incidents board and will follow up on the quota ticket until resolved.

infra-bot: [Resolved] Incident closed at 1778006600. Root cause: runaway ad-hoc finetune job + nodepool label/taint mismatch preventing effective cluster-autoscaler scale-up.

Lee: Great work. We'll circle back in the postmortem to tighten notebook UX and autoscaler templates. :pray:
